title: OpenID Connect
note: No long-lived cloud secrets; short-lived token valid for a single job; trust conditions match subject claims, example repo:octo-org/octo-repo:environment:prod; repositories created after 15 July 2026 use an immutable subject format with owner and repository IDs

title: Secure use reference
note: Pin actions to a commit SHA, or lock workflow dependencies with a lockfile which supersedes SHA pinning; least privilege GITHUB_TOKEN; avoid pull_request_target unless necessary

title: Deployments and environments
note: Up to six required reviewers, one approval suffices, initiator cannot approve own deployment; environment secrets only after approval; on Free, Pro and Team required reviewers and wait timers only in public repositories

title: Dependabot options reference
note: ecosystem values npm, pip, uv, github-actions, docker; schedule interval/day/time/timezone/cronjob; groups; cooldown; open-pull-requests-limit default 5, security 10; commit-message; labels

title: GitHub flow
note: A lightweight, branch-based workflow: create branch, make changes, open pull request, address review comments, merge, delete branch.

title: Troubleshooting required status checks
note: Workflows skipped by path filtering, branch filtering or a commit message: associated checks stay Pending and block merging; avoid requiring workflows that can be skipped. A job skipped by a conditional reports Success

title: About rulesets
note: rulesets aggregate, most restrictive wins, layer with branch protection, active/disabled, bypass list, visible to anyone with read access

title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
note: Five metrics. Throughput: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time. Instability: change fail rate, deployment rework rate. Page last updated 5 January 2026.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
note: 2025 edition: LLM01 Prompt Injection ... LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption

title: Node.js Release Working Group repository
note: Read directly while building the skill (not a playbook source); release schedule and LTS policy.

title: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0
note: changelogs are for humans; Unreleased section at top; change types Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security; do not dump git logs

title: Continuous Integration
note: Each member merges changes into the shared codebase at least daily; each integration verified by an automated build with tests. Updated 18 January 2024.

title: Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags), by Pete Hodgson
note: release, experiment, ops and permissioning toggles; release toggles short-lived; toggles are inventory with carrying cost; removal tasks and expiry dates

title: Continuous Delivery
note: CD: software can be released to production at any time. Continuous deployment: every change goes to production automatically. CD is a prerequisite for continuous deployment. 30 May 2013.

title: ParallelChange, by Danilo Sato
note: expand, migrate, contract phases for backward-incompatible interface changes; skipping contract leaves you worse off

title: A successful Git branching model (note of reflection, 5 March 2020)
note: Author says teams doing continuous delivery should adopt a much simpler workflow such as GitHub flow; git-flow may still fit explicitly versioned software or multiple supported versions.

title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
note: MAJOR incompatible API changes, MINOR backward compatible functionality, PATCH backward compatible fixes; 0.y.z anything may change; deprecate in a minor release before removal in a major

title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 14: Managing Incidents
note: roles incident command, operational work, communication, planning; declare early; criteria

title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 6: Monitoring Distributed Systems
note: four golden signals latency, traffic, errors, saturation; every page should be actionable; frequent pages get ignored

title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 15: Postmortem Culture
note: blameless definition; triggers; contents

title: OWASP Top 10:2025
note: A01 Broken Access Control, A02 Security Misconfiguration, A03 Software Supply Chain Failures, A04 Cryptographic Failures, A05 Injection, A06 Insecure Design, A07 Authentication Failures, A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures, A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures, A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions

title: Trunk Based Development
note: Developers collaborate on a single branch called trunk and resist long-lived branches; short-lived feature branches reviewed and built before landing.

title: Conventional Commits 1.0.0
note: type(scope): description; fix to PATCH, feat to MINOR, BREAKING CHANGE or ! to MAJOR
